correctness.rationale: Every deletion-cover failure at y forces C⊆F_y (y-avoiding family). F_y can be an insertion cover iff no (m+2R)-word forces every length (m+R) subsequence to contain y. Explicit forcing words for all reversal/complement orbits m<=3 and for every length-four pattern except 0110,1001 establish the first separating length. The nontrivial witness z=00(10)^(R+1) for y=0010 has longest avoiding subsequence at most R+3, below R+4; alternating/run witnesses cover remaining orbits. For 0110, Xie–Sun–Ge’s balanced-symbol contradiction shows F_0110 insertion covering; complementation proves F_1001. Greedy completion shows F_y covers every deletion target other than y, hence inclusion maximal and exhausts all maximal counterexamples. Counting greedy prefix advances gives Σ binom(n,j), j<=3. The source proof has correct quantifier directions and carefully distinguishes inclusion maximality from minimum code size. Independently implemented exact finite subsequence DP for R=1..4 and m=1..4, finding exactly the two exceptional patterns at m=4; all-radius assertion is proved by explicit templates, not finite experiments.
residual_risks: Exact binary alphabet, scattered subsequences, R>=1, n>R. Inclusion maximal means no proper containing insertion-but-not-deletion family, not minimum-cardinality code; classification only at first separating length.

final_claim: For binary scattered-subsequence covering of exact radius R>=1, each R-insertion covering code of length R<n<=R+3 is also an R-deletion covering code. At n=R+4 the only inclusion-maximal R-insertion but not R-deletion covering families are F_0110 and F_1001, consisting of words avoiding the displayed length-four scattered pattern; their common cardinality is Σ_{j=0}^3 binom(R+4,j).
limitations: Exact binary alphabet, scattered subsequences, R>=1, n>R. Inclusion maximal means no proper containing insertion-but-not-deletion family, not minimum-cardinality code; classification only at first separating length.
